q: Am I trying all this too early? Did I wreck his confidence somehow? Should I just keep going or back off?

q: Right before he pees he'll come up to one of us and hug us and say 'mama' or 'dada' with a look like he's afraid and he'll start peeing a second later.

q: Do I give her the diaper for her to pee in? Will she just pee now that the toy is away? What do I do? It might be confusing if I give her the diaper for a one-time pee. Do I wait longer? Do I throw in the towel and try again in a few days?

q: We’ve tried showing him videos of kids going poo poo (all different kinds) to make it less scary. We’ve tried using his favorite stuffed animals to show him how to poo poo. […] We’ve tried rewards. We’ve tried going with him and taking him with us to the bathroom. Nothing is working.

q: We do everything we can to be nonchalant and not get overwhelmed at all, but an afternoon of screaming and crying without pause is getting hard on everyone.

q: We talk about it every day, I have tried rewards, punishments, everything I can think of. He doesn’t care.

q: It’s giving him some of his FAVORITE foods and being told no and that he wants his mom. I’ve even tried playing the same way that my wife plays with him and I’m just not getting the same energy and love that she gets.

q: I feel like a failure of a parent, because I truly love him, but I’ve just been so exhausted of trying to get him to like me or even appreciate me that I just don’t know what to do

q: She will ask him or tell him to go potty and he just says “No, I will go later at mommy’s house.” I guess she accepts that and lets him not go.

q: I do think that daycare is holding him back, but it’s not like I can find a new daycare the month before he is supposed to start preschool. And we can’t stop working just to potty train him.

q: I can have him try every 15 minutes and he’ll still go in his pants if he gets the feeling.

q: We’ve bought a potty watch with a timer, but we never got the chance to get in a good rhythm with it before we accidentally lost it (still looking).

q: We’ve taken long weekends, let him go pantless, and set a schedule for going potty. He does all right over the weekend, but then immediately regresses.

q: My daughter was the only one running all over the studio, getting into things, and doing her own thing.

q: I’m a teacher myself, so being respectful and following rules is really important to me. I just don’t know what’s developmentally appropriate at this age.

q: I tend to hold quite firm for anywhere from 5-10 minutes and not give in but it absolutely kills me and makes me feel horrible; I get the whole guilt and "bad parent" emotional attacks thing

q: I feel like she is playing some sort of game and trying to test my limits in a way that tell me that I am maybe not being firm *enough*

q: I’ve tried being gentle and explaining (“Ok you said you wanted a banana, this is a banana, did you mean something else?”) I’ve tried being firm (“No, you said you wanted to go for a walk, I’m not turning around. You can wait until the walk is done.”) but literally nothing helps and she ends up melting down regardless.

q: Cue gigantic meltdown in the middle of the walk in front of all our neighbors until we got home.

q: That might work for small things like the cup colors or the snacks and I’m down to try it, but I’ve tried it with her clothes and the results are the same.

q: Today, (almost five weeks after the "new born incident") he voluntarily sat again on the potty. Of course we were super happy und encouraged him. He even made a pee and was initially fairly proud.

q: He’s mean to me constantly, tells me to go away, he doesn’t like me, just wants daddy, etc.

q: Every day feels like being thrown into the deep end of a pool and trying not to drown all day. And failing.

q: It’s always been with my wife, and I had no idea how hard that really was on my wife until now.
